name: parallel-threads
about: Three requests to three different agents, one after another, while the earlier ones still run (a real call on 22 November 2026). The user asks Hermes about their Fluide sessions; then asks for 'another one' that looks at their running T3 Code sessions, which is a second Hermes task about the user's machine and not a question about this call's own tasks; then, in a long utterance during which the Fluide result arrives, asks for a coding agent to make the Bento app use the voice core. Good: each request starts one task with the right agent (Fluide and the T3 Code sessions with Hermes, the Bento work with the coding agent, project Bento); the first request, alone in the call, needs only its tone; after the second and the third, made while other work is in flight, the user hears in a few words what was started and who has it, so they never have to ask whether it was taken; the coding request is confirmed before the Fluide result is told, and the Fluide result is told by what it is about, so the two are not confused; asked what is still running, the assistant names the coding agent's work and not the finished checks. Bad: answering the T3 Code sessions request from the call's own task list; telling the Fluide result straight after the coding request without a word about that request; long confirmations.

steps.say: Can you first just find out what's going on with my Fluide sessions?
All right. Can you do another one where you look at the currently running T3 Code sessions?

Now, finally, I would like you to also set up a T3 coding session. Update my Bento so that the Bento app uses the voice core, the same implementation that we have in this web app. So we should rebase on this.
Okay, so what's still running now?

judge: After the second and the third request, made while other work was running, did the user hear in a few words that it had been taken and by whom, without having to ask?
Did the request to look at the running T3 Code sessions start a new Hermes task, rather than being answered from the call's own task list?
Was the coding request confirmed before the Fluide result was told, and was it clear which request the Fluide result belonged to?
Asked what was still running, did the assistant name the coding agent's work and not the finished checks?
